parallel_group.prompt:
Make the council execution lock admit several concurrent WORKER processes on one store while still excluding a migration.

FILES YOU OWN (touch no others): src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/execlock.py and tests/domains/ai/council/test_execlock.py.

BACKGROUND. The council engine is being split so that one worker process serves one 'queue' (a named set of council seats) instead of one worker serving every seat. Today ExecutionLock uses a SINGLE lock file in the store's directory (LOCK_FILENAME, around line 55) with a closed set of holder kinds LOCK_KINDS = ('daemon', 'run', 'evaluate', 'migrate') (around line 61), acquired exclusively via flock in acquire() (around line 114). One exclusive holder per store directory means a second worker cannot start, which blocks the whole redesign.

WHY THIS IS SAFE, and you must preserve the reasoning in the docstring. The module docstring currently justifies the exclusive lock with two reasons: (a) two workers would claim the same calls, and (b) a migration would change the schema under a running worker. Reason (a) is ALREADY guaranteed elsewhere and does not need this lock: claims are taken under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a per-row claim_token and a `status == 'pending'` guard in the UPDATE (see store/queries.py claim_update, around line 236), so no two workers can take the same call for any number of workers. Reason (b) has no other backstop, which is why migrate must stay exclusive.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. A partition-scoped lock file. In addition to the store-wide lock file, a worker may take a lock file whose name includes a partition name, e.g. council-<partition>.lock alongside council.lock. Add an optional partition argument to the lock (constructor or acquire, your choice -- document it) and compute the path from it.
2. Shared vs exclusive. Worker kinds ('daemon', 'run') take the STORE-WIDE lock in SHARED mode (fcntl.flock with LOCK_SH) and, when a partition is named, ALSO take their own partition lock EXCLUSIVELY. 'migrate' takes the store-wide lock EXCLUSIVELY. 'evaluate' keeps its current behaviour.
3. LockHeld must name EVERY shared holder, not the first one. With one holder the old message named one pid; with N shared holders an operator who is told about only one will kill it, retry, and be refused again. The holder record already carries pid, kind, start time and store path -- keep writing one JSON line per holder and have the refusal message list them all. For a partition lock, the message must also name the partition.
4. An unknown kind must still raise ValueError naming LOCK_KINDS, and an unparseable holder line must still come back as {'kind': 'unknown', ...} rather than None.

TESTS TO ADD (external behaviour only -- do not assert on private attributes):
- two workers naming DIFFERENT partitions both acquire successfully and both hold at once;
- two workers naming the SAME partition: the second is refused with LockHeld naming the partition and the first holder's pid;
- 'migrate' is refused while any worker holds its shared lock, and the refusal names every holder;
- a worker acquires after a previous holder's process died without releasing (the kernel releases flock on process death -- there is no TTL and nothing should be stranded);
- the existing single-holder behaviours still hold.

CONSTRAINT: do not change the lock's public call shape for existing callers that pass no partition -- daemon.py, the CLI run path and evaluate() all call it today and are NOT yours to edit in this task.

Background reference, possibly unreachable from your worktree: agent-io/prds/council-per-seat-queues-v1/fullprompt.md on branch wip, section 'Execution locking' and Q1.

CONFRONT ROUND 1 -- BINDING AMENDMENTS (these override the paragraphs above where they differ).
(a) KEEP THE EXISTING LOCK FILE NAME. The store-wide lock must retain its current `daemon.lock` name and inode. Do NOT rename it to `council.lock`: an old binary and a new binary would each take 'the' store lock under a different name and never see each other, which is a silent double-council.
(b) THE PARTITION LOCK IS PER (queue_name, worker_index), NOT PER QUEUE. A queue may declare `workers: 2`, and if the lock is `council-<queue>.lock` every child of that queue contends for the same exclusive file so only one can ever start. Use indices 0..workers-1 and make the lock exclusive per (queue_name, index), held alongside the shared store-wide lock.
(c) ENUMERATE EVERY HOLDER. Keep holder metadata in the worker lock files, and make a store-wide refusal list every kernel-held worker lock rather than the first one.
(d) EXCLUSIVITY FOR THE LEGACY PATHS IS UNCHANGED. Unpartitioned `run`, an old-style `daemon`, and `evaluate` all remain EXCLUSIVE on the store-wide lock, so they cannot coexist with queue workers in either direction. Shared mode is only for a queue child launched under the controller.
(e) ADD A CONTROLLER LOCK KIND. There is one persistent exclusive controller lock per store; queue workers are only ever launched beneath it. Add whatever kind is needed to LOCK_KINDS for that.
Add tests for (b) -- two children of one queue with distinct indices both acquire -- and for (c) and (d).
parallel_group.success_criteria: test_execlock.py contains tests that (a) two distinct partitions hold concurrently, (b) the same partition is refused with LockHeld naming the partition, (c) migrate is refused while a shared worker lock is held and the message names every holder, and (d) a dead holder's lock is immediately re-acquirable; all of these pass on the branch, and no test that passed on the base commit fails on the branch.

phases.name: Store claim filter and additive schema

parallel_group.prompt:
Let a council worker claim only the calls belonging to its own seats, and add the two additive schema changes the rest of this PRD needs.

PART 1 -- CLAIM FILTER. select_claimable(endpoints, now, limit, *, identity) in store/queries.py (around line 164) filters on calls.status == 'pending', due-ness, calls.endpoint.in_(endpoints), job status and halts. parallel_group.prompt:
Add a `queues` section to the council configuration, and make it REFUSE a configuration that would over-subscribe a provider account.

FILES YOU OWN (touch no others): src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/config.py and tests/domains/ai/council/test_types_config.py.

CONTEXT YOU NEED FROM THE EXISTING FILE. EndpointConfig (around line 549) carries `account` (around 573) and `max_concurrency` (around 574), with a default applied when absent (around 634) from DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY by endpoint kind. CouncilConfig (around 672) holds `endpoints`, `models` and `profiles`, and those three sections are merged PER ENTRY by the loader (around line 903) rather than wholesale -- `queues` must follow that same merge rule.

WHY THIS MATTERS. The engine is being split into one worker process per named queue, where a queue serves a set of SEATS. Concurrency, however, is owned by the provider ACCOUNT, not the seat: in the live roster two council chairs (gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-terra) both sit on the `codex` endpoint and therefore the same account. If two codex queues each declared concurrency 8 against an account capped at 8, they would open 16 concurrent children and get rate-limited. Validating this at config load is what makes runtime coordination between worker processes unnecessary -- so this validation is load-bearing, not a nicety.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. A QueueConfig model with fields: `seats` (list of seat names, required, non-empty); `roles` (optional list, restricting the queue to those roles); `workers` (int, default 1); `concurrency` (int, required); `batch_size` (int, default 1); `max_output_tokens_per_item` (optional int).
2. `queues: Dict[str, QueueConfig] = {}` on CouncilConfig, merged per entry exactly as endpoints/models/profiles are.
3. VALIDATION, raising the error type this module already uses for bad configuration (match the existing style -- do not invent a new exception):
   - no seat may appear in more than one queue. The error must name the seat and both queues. (Two queues on one seat does not corrupt anything -- the claim protocol prevents double-claiming the same call -- it silently counts that seat's concurrency against the account twice, which is far harder to diagnose than a refusal.)
   - `batch_size >= 1` and `workers >= 1` and `concurrency >= 1`.
   - `batch_size > 1` is permitted only for a seat whose endpoint kind is one of the CLI kinds (the batchable backends); otherwise refuse, naming the seat and its kind.
   - FOR EACH ACCOUNT: sum over queues whose seats resolve to that account of (queue.concurrency * queue.workers) must be <= that account's max_concurrency. The error must name the account, its cap, the computed sum, and every contributing queue. Resolve a seat to its account by way of the seat's endpoint and that endpoint's `account` (falling back to the per-endpoint default the existing code uses when `account` is absent).
4. Add a `cli_temp_root` option (optional path) in whatever section of this config the CLI-related options already live, or on CouncilConfig if there is no better home. Another task consumes it; you only declare it.
5. A config declaring NO `queues` must behave exactly as today. This section is additive and opt-in.

TESTS in test_types_config.py:
- a four-queue config (three chair queues, one combined critic/meta queue) loads and round-trips;
- a seat in two queues is refused, with both queue names in the message;
- two queues on one account summing above its cap are refused, with the account, the cap, the sum and the queue names in the message;
- the same two queues summing exactly to the cap are ACCEPTED (boundary);
- workers multiplies into the sum (2 workers x concurrency 5 counts as 10);
- batch_size > 1 on a non-CLI seat is refused;
- a config with no `queues` loads and is unchanged from today;
- the per-entry merge rule applies to `queues` (an override of one queue does not drop its siblings).

Background reference, possibly unreachable from your worktree: agent-io/prds/council-per-seat-queues-v1/fullprompt.md on branch wip, section 'Queue configuration' and Q4.

CONFRONT ROUND 1 -- BINDING AMENDMENTS (these override the paragraphs above where they differ).
(a) A SEAT NAME DOES NOT BIND TO ONE ACCOUNT. CouncilConfig.roster(profile, overrides) resolves seat names per job: `overrides` is keyed by SEAT NAME and the special key "proposers" REPLACES THE PROPOSER BENCH ENTIRELY (config.py around :725-:760). So `proposer_1` can reach different accounts in two simultaneous jobs. Validating only the default profile would make the no-over-commitment promise FALSE. Resolve EVERY declared profile and charge each queue's full concurrency*workers reservation to EVERY account it can reach. An account's cap is the MINIMUM effective endpoint cap for that account (the worker already computes a min this way, engine/worker.py:362).
(b) COVERAGE IS REQUIRED. Queue mode requires exactly one owner for every executable (seat_name, role) in every accepted roster, with NO implicit fallback worker. Refuse an uncovered pair at load -- otherwise a valid-looking config that omits `meta` or filters out a role produces a job that silently never finishes.
(c) EVERY QUEUE MUST RESOLVE TO EXACTLY ONE ACCOUNT. Refuse a multi-account queue. This makes 'one account per queue' an enforced invariant instead of a convention, and removes the undefined question of whether `concurrency` on a multi-account queue is an aggregate or a per-account allocation.
(d) batch_size IS 1..50 WITH A DEFAULT OF 1, and there is NO seat-level batch_size field in this version; a queue's value applies independently to each of its seats. 20 is the value an operator writes for a Claude queue, not a default.
(e) Add the rejection hook contract for (a): submission-time and pre-claim validation of a roster/override against the validated set, with a diagnostic naming the job and seat, and NO mutation of stored calls on refusal. If the natural home for that check is outside config.py, define the predicate here and report where the caller must invoke it rather than editing another module.
Add tests for (a) with a profile override that moves a seat to another account, for (b) with a config omitting meta, and for (c).
parallel_group.success_criteria: A four-queue config loads and round-trips; a duplicate seat, an over-subscribed account, and batch_size>1 on a non-CLI seat are each refused with a message naming the specific offending items; a config summing exactly to an account cap is accepted; `workers` multiplies into the account sum; a config with no `queues` section loads with behaviour unchanged from the base commit; and no test that passed on the base commit fails on the branch.

parallel_group.prompt:
Make CouncilWorker serve ONE queue (a set of seats), fix the two concurrency-budget bugs that caused the production starvation, and make per-seat service time measurable.

FILES YOU OWN (touch no others): src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/engine/worker.py and tests/domains/ai/council/test_engine.py.

THE STARVATION, WITH ITS MECHANISM AND ITS NUMBERS. _free_slots() (around line 901) sums free capacity across EVERY account the worker serves. That total becomes the `limit` handed to store.claim_calls(). But the claim query returns the GLOBAL queue head with no per-account quota, so a saturated account's rows occupy the entire batch. Then _claim() (around line 905) increments _AccountLimit.assigned UNCONDITIONALLY (around line 923), so `assigned` runs past `capacity`, which drives _free_slots() to zero and stalls every other account behind the saturated one. Measured on the live store: 92 calls claimed against ~20 slots, 66 of them held by one account, while another account that was succeeding 52/52 held 5 and made no progress.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. PARTITION. Add optional `seats` and `roles` to CouncilWorker.__init__ and pass them to store.claim_calls(), which has gained matching optional parameters. CRITICAL: do NOT change the signature of _claim(limit, job_id, summary). daemon.py subclasses CouncilWorker and overrides _claim, calling super() with exactly those three arguments; it is NOT yours to edit in this task and a signature change breaks it. Carry seats/roles as worker attributes instead.

2. PER-ACCOUNT CLAIMING. _free_slots() must stop returning a cross-account sum. Claim per account: for each account with free capacity, ask for at most that account's free slots. The simplest correct shape is a claim per account limit; if you keep one call, you must still never ask for more than one account's free slots at a time.

3. assigned MUST NEVER EXCEED capacity. A row arriving for an account already at capacity is released immediately through the existing _release_quietly path (which releases with increment_attempt=False -- nothing is wrong with the call) and counted in summary['released'].

4. SERVICE TIME. In _invoke (around line 1173) `started = _utcnow()` is stamped BEFORE `async with self._slot(endpoint)` on the next line, so every stored elapsed is queue-wait PLUS service time conflated. This is why two honest measurements of the same seat disagreed by 65x. Move `started` to AFTER the slot is acquired, and capture a second timestamp when the call ENTERED the slot queue. Write it to the `attempts.queued_at` column that another task has already added (nullable; absence means 'nothing to say'). After this change service time is finished_at - started_at and queue wait is started_at - queued_at.

5. TEMP ROOT WIRING. The config now declares a CLI temp root and run_cli now accepts an optional `temp_root` parameter. Thread the configured value through to the backend invocation so a CLI child's working directory is created under it. When unconfigured, behaviour is unchanged.

PRESERVE, because each exists for a reason stated in the code: the out-of-scope job release in _claim (the claim contract has no job filter, so handing a foreign job's row straight back unmarked is the only way to scope a run); the set_job_status(..., only_if=('queued',)) transition on claim; _run_one's decrement of assigned in a finally; the re-raise of a worker bug out of work() rather than swallowing it; and the gather of in-flight calls in work()'s finally (claimed calls are already paid for).

TESTS in test_engine.py, using the existing scripted-fake backend support in engine_support.py:
- THE STARVATION REGRESSION TEST, and it must FAIL on the base commit -- a test that passes before the fix is testing nothing. Two accounts, one slow and saturated, one fast and free, with the slow account's rows at the FIFO head. Assert the fast account's calls complete while the slow account's are still in flight.
- `assigned` never exceeds `capacity` for any account across a claim storm with far more pending rows than slots.
- a partitioned worker (seats={A}) never runs a call for seat B even when B's rows are at the queue head.
- queued_at is written, and started_at is at or after queued_at, and for a call that waited for a slot started_at is strictly later.
- the unpartitioned worker (no seats, no roles) behaves as on the base commit.

Background reference, possibly unreachable from your worktree: agent-io/prds/council-per-seat-queues-v1/fullprompt.md on branch wip, sections 'Per-queue worker and budget' and 'Service-time instrumentation'.

CONFRONT ROUND 1 -- BINDING AMENDMENTS (these override the paragraphs above where they differ).
(a) THE PER-CHILD BUDGET IS queue.concurrency, NOT the account's max_concurrency. _build_limits currently builds full account capacities; under queue mode the child's budget is its queue's own number.
(b) FOR A BATCHED QUEUE, FREE CAPACITY IS MEASURED IN INVOCATIONS, NOT ROWS. The row-bounded claim and 'a batch is one in-flight unit' are otherwise in direct conflict: at concurrency 1 a row-bounded claim yields one row forever and a batch of 20 can never form; at concurrency 8 per-row assignment prevents a 20-row batch. So when the queue's batch_size > 1: claim up to free_slots * effective_batch_size CANDIDATE rows, group them by the complete homogeneity key, schedule no more than free_slots batches, release surplus groups WITHOUT incrementing attempts, and increment `assigned` ONCE when a batch is reserved. An unbatched queue keeps the per-row free_slots bound exactly.
(c) Batch ASSEMBLY and settlement themselves are the next task's work; this task must leave the claim loop able to hand a GROUP of homogeneous rows to the execution path, rather than assuming one row per launched task (the loop currently launches one task per claimed row, around :799 and :937).
Add a test that at concurrency 1 with batch_size 20 a full batch can still be assembled.
parallel_group.success_criteria: test_engine.py contains a two-account starvation test that fails on the base commit and passes on the branch; `assigned` is proven never to exceed `capacity` under a claim storm; a seat-partitioned worker never executes another seat's call; `attempts.queued_at` is populated with started_at >= queued_at and strictly later when a slot was contended; the _claim(limit, job_id, summary) signature is unchanged from the base commit; an unpartitioned worker's behaviour is unchanged; and no test that passed on the base commit fails on the branch.

parallel_group.prompt:
Make the council daemon supervise one worker process per configured queue, and report and stop them per queue.

FILES YOU OWN (touch no others): src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/daemon.py and tests/domains/ai/council/test_daemon.py.

WHAT EXISTS. CouncilDaemon already spawns a detached child: start() around line 411 and _default_child_argv() around line 483. stop() around line 524 implements a bounded drain whose contract is load-bearing and must be preserved exactly: SIGTERM stops claiming and lets in-flight calls finish for up to DaemonTimings.drain_s, then unfinished HTTP tasks are cancelled, every unfinished CLI process GROUP is killed and reaped, and each still-claimed call is -- in ONE transaction -- given an 'interrupted' attempt, has its claim token invalidated, and goes back to pending WITHOUT its retry count moving (see _interrupt_claimed around line 779). A daemon being stopped is not the call's fault; spending retry budget on an operator restart is how a long batch dies of attrition.

Also preserve: the chdir into the council directory before serving anything (both CLI backends read project context from the cwd, so inheriting a caller's worktree would put that repository in scope for council answers), and the per-(endpoint, served model) readiness probing -- _admits around line 938, _routes around line 1165 -- including _DaemonWorker._claim's hand-back of a row its route cannot run and the slot-giveback that stops the budget leaking one slot per rejected claim.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. ONE CHILD PER QUEUE. The config now has a `queues` section; each entry names `seats`, optional `roles`, `workers` (how many processes), `concurrency` and `batch_size`. start() launches `workers` children per queue, extending _default_child_argv with the queue name so each child serves exactly its own queue. Each child constructs its worker with that queue's seats/roles and concurrency.
2. LOCKING. ExecutionLock now supports a partition: worker kinds take the store-wide lock SHARED and their own partition lock EXCLUSIVELY. Each queue child takes the partition lock for its queue name. Two children of the same queue (workers > 1) need distinct partition names -- derive them from the queue name plus an index.
3. STATUS PER QUEUE. status() must aggregate per queue: child pid, whether it is alive, and for that queue's seats the claimed / in-flight / pending counts and the last heartbeat. 'Nothing is moving' must name WHICH queue.
4. PER-QUEUE STOP AND START. Accept a queue name: stopping one queue drains and stops only its children and leaves its siblings running; starting one queue starts only its children. A stop with no queue named stops everything, as today.
5. NO `queues` CONFIG means exactly today's behaviour -- a single unpartitioned child over all seats.

TESTS in test_daemon.py, following the shape already there (do not spawn real model calls):
- a four-queue config starts four children, each with its own queue name in its argv;
- workers: 2 on a queue starts two children with distinct partition lock names, and both acquire;
- status() reports per-queue counts, and a queue with pending work and a dead child is distinguishable from a queue with nothing to do;
- stopping one queue leaves the others running and claiming;
- the bounded-drain contract still holds: a still-claimed call at the deadline gets an 'interrupted' attempt and returns to pending with its attempt_count UNCHANGED;
- a config with no `queues` starts exactly one child covering all seats, as on the base commit.

Background reference, possibly unreachable from your worktree: agent-io/prds/council-per-seat-queues-v1/fullprompt.md on branch wip, section 'Daemon supervision'.

CONFRONT ROUND 1 -- BINDING AMENDMENTS (these override the paragraphs above where they differ).
(a) SPAWNING DETACHED CHILDREN IS NOT SUPERVISION. Today's detached child IS the daemon and the caller exits once it has verified the child's lock (daemon.py:411), so N detached daemons leave no process able to restart a dead one -- and the death-recovery requirement would be unmeetable. ONE DETACHED CONTROLLER MUST REMAIN ALIVE and supervise the workers.
(b) RESTART POLICY. An UNEXPECTED worker exit triggers claim recovery through the existing stale-worker lease and a restart after 5 seconds, indefinitely, with the failure visible in status(). A DELIBERATE per-queue stop disables restart for that queue until an explicit start -- an operator's stop must never be undone by the supervisor.
(c) INITIAL START IS ALL-OR-NOTHING. If any child fails readiness, drain and stop every child started by that operation and return failure. Leaving two of three queues consuming work after a partial start is a materially worse outcome than failing cleanly.
(d) FOREGROUND MODE RUNS THE SAME CONTROLLER attached to the terminal, so the two paths do not diverge.
(e) THE CONTROLLER HOLDS AN EXCLUSIVE CONTROLLER LOCK and is the only thing that may launch queue workers; a standalone `run` in queue mode is REFUSED. Its active queue configuration is IMMUTABLE while any of its workers is running -- a change requires stop-all then start-all. This is what actually preserves the account guarantee: static config validation counts only ONE config's reservations, so two processes from different queue configs could otherwise hold non-conflicting partition locks and jointly over-commit a provider. Claim tokens do not prevent provider over-commitment.
(f) Child argv carries the queue name AND the worker index (locks are per (queue, index)).
Add tests for (b) both ways, for (c), and for (e)'s refusal of a standalone queue-mode run.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A four-queue config starts four children each carrying its queue name; a queue with workers=2 starts two children holding distinct partition locks; status() reports per-queue claimed/in-flight/pending and distinguishes a dead child from an idle queue; stopping one queue leaves siblings claiming; a still-claimed call at the drain deadline returns to pending with attempt_count unchanged from before the stop; a config with no `queues` starts one child over all seats as on the base commit; and no test that passed on the base commit fails on the branch.

parallel_group.prompt:
Let a CLI seat answer up to N items in ONE backend invocation, settling each item's call row independently.

FILES YOU OWN (touch no others): src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/engine/worker.py, src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/queries/spec.py (the render/answer-schema surface), and tests/domains/ai/council/ -- add a new test module for batching rather than enlarging test_engine.py.

WHY. Each `claude -p` invocation carries roughly 7,500 tokens of CLI harness before a ~300-token question, so about 96% of billed input is boilerplate paid once per item. Per-item input is 7500/n + 300: at n=1 that is ~7,800 tokens, at n=20 it is ~675, an 11.6x reduction, and 38,552 calls become 1,928. Output does NOT amortize (~667 tokens per item regardless), so after this change output is the dominant cost.

MEASURE FIRST, AND RECORD WHAT YOU MEASURE. Two numbers in this PRD were derived from a SINGLE stored usage record because `claude -p` could not be executed during authoring: the ~7,500-token harness floor, and the claim that a ~16K output budget supports a 20-item batch at ~667 output tokens per item. Before trusting the default, measure the real per-item output and the real harness floor for the seat you enable, and write both into the task's work record. If they contradict the PRD, the derived ceiling below must still make the outcome a REDUCED BATCH, never a truncation.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. BATCH ASSEMBLY. A batch is a set of claimed call rows sharing (job_id, role, seat_name, query_name, query_version). Homogeneity is free because a partitioned worker's claim is already single-seat, but ASSERT it rather than assuming it. Size: n = min(batch_size, rows_in_hand, derived_ceiling) where derived_ceiling = floor(seat.max_output_tokens * 0.75 / per_item_output). per_item_output comes from the config's max_output_tokens_per_item when set, else a running mean of observed per-item output for that (seat, role); with NEITHER available, force batch_size to 1 -- batching must never run on an unknown. Fewer rows in hand than batch_size simply means the batch is the rows in hand. Log once per (seat, run) when derived_ceiling < batch_size, naming both numbers, so a silently-reduced batch is visible.

2. REQUEST SHAPE. The rendered user content becomes a numbered list of per-item blocks, each carrying an opaque `item_key`. The answer schema becomes an object with an `answers` array whose elements each carry their `item_key` plus the EXISTING per-role answer shape unchanged. The system prompt gains only a statement that every answer must carry back its item_key and that items are independent.

3. SETTLEMENT GOES 1:N. Resolve each returned element to its call row by item_key, validate it against the EXISTING per-role answer schema so _validate_answer and engine/normalise.py are reused UNCHANGED per element, and settle that row through the existing _settle_ok path. Handle each of these explicitly:
   - MISSING element: the row is released for retry with attempt_count INCREMENTED. A model answering 18 of 20 must bank 18.
   - UNKNOWN item_key not in the batch: dropped with a warning, never written.
   - DUPLICATE item_key: first wins, duplicate dropped with a warning.
   - USAGE: one invocation returns one usage record. Record it ONCE on the batch's first call row together with the batch size and the member call_ids; the remaining rows get a zero-cost attempt referencing it. DO NOT divide it N ways -- that would invent per-item token counts the provider never reported, and those invented numbers would then feed the next batch's ceiling.
   - BUDGET: a batch is ONE in-flight unit against _AccountLimit. `assigned` moves by one per batch, not by N.

4. BISECTION ON FAILURE. A failure that is not per-item (transport, timeout, truncation, top-level schema-invalid) is retried by splitting the batch in half and re-running each half, recursing down to single items. Bisection consumes one attempt per ITEM, not one per batch, so a poison item is isolated in log2(n) rounds and the other items still settle. A single item failing alone fails exactly as it does today.

5. REUSE STAYS PER ITEM -- THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION IS WRONG. prompt_hash must continue to be computed from the SINGLE-ITEM rendered prompt for that call row, NEVER from the batch. Batching changes only the transport. Hashing what you actually sent would make the key depend on which other items happened to ride along, silently destroying cross-job reuse of already-paid answers -- the property that makes a roster change cheap. _reusable_self and find_reusable must keep working.

6. batch_size defaults to 1, which must be bit-for-bit today's behaviour for any seat not opted in.

TESTS, all against the scripted fake backend so no subscription is spent:
- N rows settle from one reply;
- a reply missing two item_keys settles N-2 and releases 2 with attempt_count incremented;
- an unknown item_key is dropped and nothing is written for it;
- a duplicate item_key takes the first;
- usage is recorded once, carrying batch size and member call_ids, with zero-cost attempts on the rest;
- _AccountLimit.assigned moves by one per batch, not N;
- bisection: a fake that fails any batch containing a designated poison item settles every other item and charges the poison item its own attempts;
- derived ceiling: an unknown per-item output forces batch_size 1, and a ceiling below batch_size reduces the batch and logs both numbers;
- REUSE: an item answered inside a batch is afterwards reusable by prompt_hash from a DIFFERENT job;
- batch_size 1 reproduces base-commit behaviour.

Background reference, possibly unreachable from your worktree: agent-io/prds/council-per-seat-queues-v1/fullprompt.md on branch wip, section 'Batched invocation' and Q2, Q3, Q5.

CONFRONT ROUND 1 -- BINDING AMENDMENTS (these override the paragraphs above where they differ).
(a) seat.max_output_tokens IS NOT AN OUTPUT CAP FOR A CLI SEAT, AND NOTHING FORWARDS ONE. Verified: NEITHER CLI argv passes any output-token limit. So this is not a question of whether a flag is honoured -- there is no flag. CONSEQUENCE: enable batching ONLY for a CLI/model combination with a VERIFIED effective output cap and a documented mechanism for setting it; until verified, FORCE THAT COMBINATION TO SINGLES and report why. A backend declaring batch support does NOT establish an output cap. effective_output_cap is the LESSER of the verified cap and seat.max_output_tokens. A running mean is not a worst-case bound even with a real cap, so the heuristic REDUCES truncation risk rather than eliminating it; detected truncation still falls through to bisection. If no cap can be verified, the correct outcome is that this task lands with batching disabled -- that is success, not failure.
(b) derived_ceiling < 1 REFUSES batching for that seat with a diagnostic. Never assemble an empty batch; it leaves work spinning forever.
(c) VALIDATE THE WRAPPER AND KEYS SEPARATELY FROM ROLE PAYLOADS, and strip item_key before the existing role-schema validation runs. Validating the whole wrapper as one schema would reject 20 answers because one was malformed.
(d) KEYED-BUT-INVALID PAYLOAD NEEDS ITS OWN POLICY. A valid known item_key carrying a role-schema-invalid payload is treated LIKE A MISSING ANSWER, not like today's single-reply case (which is terminal, around :1198): record invalid_output and release ONLY that row with increment_attempt=True while below max_attempts; on exhaustion settle it as error and advance its item. Bank every valid unique known answer in the same reply.
(e) MISSING ANSWERS NEED A FINITE max_attempts TOO. As first written, a missing element was always released with its attempt incremented and no exhaustion rule, so an always-omitted item would consume calls indefinitely.
(f) USAGE IS ANCHORED ON A UNIQUE invocation_id, NOT ON 'the batch's first call row'. The first row may be missing, invalid or stale, and a bisected CHILD batch can share its parent's first row -- so that anchor double-counts or references an attempt that was never written. Give every backend invocation a unique invocation_id and atomically record, exactly once, its reported usage, ordered member ids, batch size and anchor (call_id, attempt_no), updating endpoint spend once -- AND DO THIS FOR FAILED INVOCATIONS TOO, whose spend today's retry path discards (see around :1394, :1491, :1520). Every member attempt references invocation_id.
(g) THE RUNNING MEAN MUST EXCLUDE ZERO-COST AND PARTIAL SAMPLES. Including zero-cost member attempts drags the per-item estimate DOWN, which ENLARGES the next batch -- a feedback loop pointed at the truncation this guard exists to prevent. Define it as total completion_tokens / total requested members over SUCCESSFUL COMPLETE invocations for the same (seat, role, served_model), excluding partial, truncated, failed, reused and unknown-usage samples. With no eligible history use the configured estimate or fresh singleton observations.
(h) BISECTION VS THE ATTEMPT BUDGET -- as first written these could not coexist. max_attempts defaults to 3 (around :282) while a path 20->10->5->3->2->1 needs FIVE failed ancestor invocations before the poison item is invoked alone, so honouring the budget would fail healthy neighbours before isolation. Also attempt_no derives from attempt_count and is part of a primary key (around :1621; store/schema.py around :290), so recursion needs real counter updates. Therefore: record and increment attempt_count for each failed ANCESTOR invocation, but DO NOT enforce the single-item max_attempts budget until a row is invoked ALONE, counting singleton failures separately from batch-isolation failures; run split halves DIRECTLY UNDER THE EXISTING CLAIMS, sequentially per reserved slot, WITHOUT returning them to the queue (a re-queued half can recombine with the poison item and loop); on worker death abandon the split tree and recover claims WITHOUT an additional failure charge; and persist enough attempt metadata that singleton failures are reconstructible across a restart.
(i) Capacity is measured in INVOCATIONS for a batched queue -- the previous task left the claim loop able to hand you a GROUP; consume that rather than re-deriving a row bound.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Batching puts up to 20 independent closed-menu classifications in one model context, where they can influence each other. parallel_group.prompt:
Make the partitioned-claim index reach stores that ALREADY EXIST. Today only brand-new stores get it.

FILES YOU OWN (touch no others): src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/store/sqlite.py, src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/store/schema.py, and the store suites under tests/domains/ai/council/ (store_contract.py, test_store_contract.py, test_store_migrate_v2.py).

THE GAP, VERIFIED BY REVIEW. An earlier phase added `ix_calls_status_seat_not_before` to support the seat-filtered claim scan. `SqliteStore.migrate()` on an already-v2 store only runs `add_missing_columns()` -- COLUMNS, not indexes -- so the index is never backfilled; it is created only via `create_all()` for new stores. And the index definition carries no `if_not_exists` flag, so running `create_all()` unconditionally would NOT safely backfill it either. An explicit `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` step is required.

Resuming that job is the whole point of this PRD. Without the index, every seat-filtered claim scans those rows and sorts them, repeatedly, for the life of the run -- so the partition fix would land and the resume would still crawl, for a reason nobody would look for.

WHAT TO BUILD. An idempotent index-backfill step that runs for an existing store as well as a fresh one -- `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` over the indexes the schema declares, applied at the same point `add_missing_columns()` is applied. Make it general over declared indexes rather than hard-coding this one index, so the next index added does not reintroduce the same gap; but keep it strictly additive.

- DO NOT BUMP SCHEMA_VERSION. It must stay 2. A bump would refuse to open every existing store, including the live one holding 104 already-paid model answers. The whole reason the column was additive was to keep that store openable.
- The backfill must be IDEMPOTENT: running it twice, or on a store that already has the index, must be a no-op and must never raise.
- It must not rebuild, drop or reorder any existing index, and must leave `ix_calls_status_not_before` in place for the unpartitioned claim path.
- It must not lock the store for a meaningful period on a large table in a way that would wedge a running worker -- state what you measured or why it is safe.

Put the behaviour in the store CONTRACT where it belongs so both implementations are covered.
